olivia: Quick follow-up from the RFC — I'm proposing a lightweight 'granularity negotiation' handshake between the compiler and runtime to decide per-request per-layer quant granularity (fp8 / int8 / 4bit) before scheduling. Wants to be cheap and cacheable. Thoughts?

samir: Do we need a new RPC for that? Could we piggyback on existing model metadata exchange during route selection? Main tradeoff I see: extra pre-inference work (latency) vs avoiding bad-quality outputs.

nina: Concern: any sync step adds tail latency. If negotiation hits the network it could add 2-10ms. Suggest we make it async + cached per model-version + prompt-shape hash so the cold path is the only painful one.

gabe: We already keep quant profiles per model version. Idea: extend the cache key with a short prompt-shape-hash and an optional 'quality-tier' header. On cache miss, runtime should fall back to a safe int8 policy, not block the request.

olivia: Agree on the fallback. Also propose we define a "degradation boundary matrix" that maps estimated quality delta -> allowed perf gain. That lets us make deterministic decisions instead of ad-hoc heuristics. Example concept matrix: 

```
# quality_delta_pct  | max_perf_gain_pct | action
0 - 0.5              | up to 30%          | allow fp8/4bit
0.5 - 1.5            | up to 15%          | allow int8 only
> 1.5                | any                | deny low-precision, use baseline fp16
```

samir: Runtime implications: kernel selection graph will grow (more edges for fp8/int8/4bit variants + fallback nodes). Need to avoid combinatorial explosion. Maybe keep negotiation coarse-grained at module-level instead of per-layer for now.

nina: Ops/rollout question: how do we canary this safely? My proposal: do canary traffic with header `X-Quant-Mode: negotiate,aggressive` for a small % and gate based on eval-set drift. If drift > 1.5% revert.

gabe: API change suggestion: add optional header `X-Quant-Preferences: fp8,int8` which signals a preference order. If header absent, runtime behaves exactly as today. Backwards compatible. Also add `X-Quant-Cache-Key: <hash>` to allow clients to opt-in to reuse negotiation decisions.

quant-ci-bot: quant-ci-bot: nightly sim run at 2109876500 finished: on `llama-13b-tilt` fp8 profile flagged 3/50 eval prompts with >1.5% metric regression (proxy CE + token-loss). Full report: https://ci.internal/reports/2109876500

olivia: Good catch @quant-ci-bot. Action items from here: 
1) Samir: spike header prototyping + cache key change (prototype + perf metric)
2) Nina: draft degradation boundary matrix + canary runbook (include rollback thresholds)
3) Gabe: telemetry hooks for prompt-shape-hash and proxy-eval integration
Please post short PR links when you have spikes. Timeline: spike by EOW, runbook draft next Wed.

samir: I'll do the spike, will instrument a tiny handshake and show microsecond budget. Notebook: https://notebooks.internal/2109876543-spike

nina: I'll draft runbook and sync with SRE/support about alerting.

gabe: I'll add telemetry events to the eval pipeline, and wire up automatic flagging for >1% drift.

olivia: Thanks all. One more note — we should keep the contract minimal: negotiation is advisory, runtime always allowed to ignore if capacity/budget demands. That keeps operators safe and avoids surprising consumers. :heavy_check_mark:
